subject: Embeddings & Reranking: Discovery Recap and Next Steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fastsearch.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings & Reranking: Discovery Recap and Next Steps

Alex — thanks again for a productive call. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive. I captured the items we discussed and a few clarifying questions below.

1) Primary pain points you shared
- Relevance drift on search results as catalog grows; current reranker only partially addresses recency/context.
- Cost spikes during campaign-driven query bursts; infra is overprovisioned to cover peak.
- Long ingestion windows for embeddings (overnight jobs cause stale vectors during daytime updates).

2) Current stack (what we heard)
- Vector DB: Pinecone (production), index: ~8M-12M vectors (est. today ~8.2M)
- Embedding model: OpenAI Ada/1536-dim for the majority of content; some internal fine-tuning for ads metadata
- Reranking: lightweight transformer reranker served on CPU autoscale; candidate recall via ANN from Pinecone
- Orchestration: nightly batch embed job (Airflow) + streams for high-priority updates

3) Workload profile & targets
- Index scale: ~8M today, growth ~1M/month (you mentioned product launches can add temporary spikes)
- Query pattern: avg QPS ~30, campaign spikes up to ~150 QPS for ~1–3 hours
- Rerank latency target: p50 < 60ms for the ANN+rerank stack, p95 goal ~150–200ms
- Cost objective: reduce per-query unit cost (network + compute) by ~2–3x vs current spend
- Batch patterns: daily full-batch ~200k embeddings, streaming updates ~2–5k/day for high-priority items

4) Success criteria you outlined
- Measured improvement in top-1/top-3 relevance on A/B test (sample eval suite)
- Achieve p95 latency <=200ms for production traffic mix
- Lowered cost per active query during steady-state and improved autoscaling for spikes

5) Clarifying questions (please confirm)
- Is the 1536-dim embedding consistent for all content or are there multiple dims in the catalog?
- Do you have a representative sample dataset (CSV + gold labels) we can use for an initial eval?
- What SLA/uptime expectations would you need for a Dedicated vs Hosted evaluation?

Next steps we propose
- Share a short sample (5k–10k rows) + a small eval script from your side so we can run a baseline on Redwood (you can drop to the Drive link above).
- Schedule a focused technical deep-dive with your eng team (proposal: Wed 18 Mar, 10:00–11:00 PT).
- Redwood to prepare a cost/latency estimate for both Hosted and Dedicated options and a 2-week POC plan.

Attachments: meeting_notes_20260315.txt (call bullets), redwood_playbook_embeddings_v1.pdf (short primer).

Thanks — if anything above needs correction, please flag and we’ll update.

—

Subject: Re: Embeddings & Reranking: Discovery Recap and Next Steps

Sean — great writeup, thanks for capturing. A few clarifications from our side:
- Index size: current production index is 8.2M vectors today (we mentioned ~12M as upper bound in six months). Growth is steady ~1M/month, but product launches can add 2–3M in a single week occasionally.
- Embeddings: 1536-dim is the default for catalog content; we also have a separate 1024-dim embedding for short metadata records (ads tags). We’d prefer a unified pipeline but can surface mixed dims if needed.
- Query mix: avg QPS ~30, normal peaks ~80–120, campaign spikes up to ~150–200 for short windows (15–180 minutes).
- Batch ingestion: nightly full run ~200k/day; streaming high-priority updates ~3–6k/day.
- Reranker: current reranker runs on small CPU fleet; it's the main bottleneck for p95 during spikes.

We can provide a sample of ~10k rows + a small label set next week. Wed 18 Mar 10:00 PT works for our engineering manager and one backend SRE. Please include an agenda that covers: sample ingestion, baseline end-to-end latency, cost model assumptions, and recommended POC scope.

Also: our internal cost target is not a fixed number yet, but we want to see a clear path to at least 2x cost reduction for steady-state queries. Happy to discuss Dedicated if the baseline shows clear latency and cost benefits.

Thanks — looking forward.

Got it — I’ll own the POC scope and will have a draft by Mon 18:00 PT. Plan:
- Scope: 2-week POC with FastSearch sample (10k rows) + eval harness (A/B slices).
- Baselines: run current Pinecone+reranker locally to get p50/p95; run Redwood hosted baseline with identical traffic profile.
- Metrics: top-k NDCG, latency (p50/p95), and estimated $/query steady-state.
- Infra notes: include quantization experiments (int8/4-bit pathways) and an autoscaling recipe for spike handling.

I’ll also add rough staffing/ops time for a Dedicated pilot so Monica’s cost sketch can include that delta.
